newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ rates seen higher if currency plunge continues.
newsitem.headline: NZ rates seen higher if currency plunge continues.

text.p: * NZ bills steady in late morning after early mayhem
* Rates seen higher if currency pluge continues to keep MCI
broadly in line with RBNZ's desired levels.

New Zealand's key 90-day bank bill rate had steadied at 8.46 percent by late Friday morning after peaking at 8.63 percent in early trade as the currency plunged over one U.S. cent to a low of US$0.6467.

The 90-day rate rocketed over 90 basis points higher than its 7.70 percent close on Thursday in an effort to offsett the Kiwi's decline and keep monetary conditions at a level acceptable to the Reserve Bank.
"We've seen debt markets respond as the Reserve Bank would have hoped they would respond to the weak currency," said Jim Reardon, senior manager domestic markets at ANZ Investment Bank.
The Monetary Conditions Index, which measures the mix of the exchange rate and the 90-day rate, opened more than 100 basis points below the RB's desired level of 825 in the September quarter.

But the rise in short-term rates brought the MCI back to 768 by 11.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) -- 57 points below the RB's desired level and only seven points outside its 50-point comfort zone. Reardon said some buying interest come back into the currency in
"So interest rates have taken some comfort from that, but any renewed selling would see renewed selling in interest rates as well."
He said rates would continue to rise if the currency fell further in order to keep monetary conditions broadly in line with the Reserve Bank's wishes.
"Until such time as the Reserve Bank comes out and condones such a move I would expect the market to respond in the appropriate fashion.
"I believe if the Kiwi continues to go lower then interest rates will go higher," he said.
